title: Remove the <blink> element from your pages
summary: The <blink> element makes text flash on and off and cannot be paused. Replace it with static text and use styling to draw attention instead.
problem: The page uses the <blink> element, an obsolete tag that makes text flash on and off. Visitors cannot pause or stop it, and modern browsers no longer support it as a standard feature of HTML.
whoItAffects: People with attention or reading difficulties, such as those with ADHD or dyslexia, find flashing text hard to read and distracting. It can also make a page uncomfortable for people with low vision.
steps: Search your templates for <blink> tags. The scan result shows the exact markup.

Replace each one with a normal element such as or

, so the text stays still.
If the text must stand out, use a static style such as bold weight or a contrasting background color.
Avoid CSS animations that make text flash, or give visitors a control to pause them.
whyItMatters: Blinking content that lasts more than five seconds must be pausable under WCAG 2.2.2 (pause, stop, hide), a Level A criterion. The <blink> element offers no way to stop it, so it fails.
howToCheck: Search the page source for the text "<blink", or watch the page for text that flashes on and off. Any match means the element is still in use.
